skill.name: imagegen
skill.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.
skill.summary: Generate, edit, validate, and save project-ready raster images with structured prompts and optional Image API controls.
skill.author: openai

security_audit.summary: Two low-severity static findings are confirmed because the CLI checks whether OPENAI_API_KEY is present; it never prints the key value. Other static findings are false positives from documentation, SVG coordinates, image decoding, dictionary methods, and non-executed backticks. The optional CLI sends selected prompts and images to OpenAI and writes outputs locally after explicit user opt-in.

remediation.issue: CLI users may provide sensitive prompts or source images to an external API.
remediation.suggestion: State near each CLI workflow that prompts and supplied images are sent to OpenAI, so users can exclude sensitive content.

content.value_statement: Producing consistent raster assets requires precise prompts, careful edits, and reliable output handling. This skill structures requests, creates or edits visuals, validates results, and saves project-ready files.
actual_capabilities: Generates new raster images through the available built-in image tool.
Edits visible or local raster images while preserving specified elements.
Structures prompts with composition, lighting, palette, exact text, and constraints.
Produces multiple variants or distinct assets and saves selected outputs.
Provides an optional OpenAI Image API CLI for generation, editing, batching, and downscaling.
limitations: Built-in availability and image quality depend on the host tool and selected model.
The optional CLI requires network access, an OpenAI API key, and installed dependencies.
Generated text, identities, labels, and fine details may require manual validation.
The skill is not intended for deterministic SVG, vector, HTML, or canvas output.

use_cases.description: Create product mockups and advertising visuals with exact copy, audience context, and layout requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [asset type] showing [subject]. Use [style] and [composition]. Avoid logos, watermarks, and unrequested text.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a first image with a clear subject and style.

prompt_templates.title: Edit One Visual Element
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit the provided [image role]. Change only [target change]. Preserve [subject, layout, colors, and details]. Save the result as [filename].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an existing image needs one controlled change.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Campaign Asset
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [campaign asset] for [audience]. Show [product] in [scene] with [lighting]. Include the exact text: "[copy]". Keep space for [layout need].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for polished marketing visuals with copy and composition requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Controlled Asset Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce [count] distinct [asset type] images for [project]. Vary [controlled dimension] while preserving [shared constraints]. Validate composition, text, and consistency. Save descriptive filenames in [directory].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for coordinated multi-asset production with controlled variation.

output_examples.input: Create a wide website hero showing a ceramic mug with soft studio lighting and clear space for copy.
output_examples.output: A wide product image with a centered ceramic mug, neutral studio background, soft shadows, and open space for page text. Saved as assets/mug-hero.png.

output_examples.input: Replace only the background of the supplied chair photo with a bright modern office.
output_examples.output: The chair remains unchanged while the background becomes a bright office with matched perspective and lighting. Saved as assets/chair-office.png.

output_examples.input: Create three consistent forest item sprites with transparent backgrounds.
output: A moss-covered potion bottle with a clean transparent edge.
A carved wooden key in the same lighting and scale.
A small leaf-wrapped compass using the shared visual style.

best_practices: State the asset purpose, subject, style, composition, and constraints before generation.
For edits, name every element that must remain unchanged.
Inspect text, edges, dimensions, and project paths before accepting the final image.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague prompts when exact layout, copy, or identity matters.
Do not replace editable vector assets with generated raster approximations.
Do not send sensitive source images through the optional CLI without reviewing external data exposure.

faq.question: Can this skill create new images?
faq.answer: Yes. It generates raster images from structured descriptions using the available image tool.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing local image?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill first loads the local image for inspection, then applies requested changes while preserving stated invariants.

faq.question: Does the default workflow require an API key?
faq.answer: No. The built-in image tool does not require OPENAI_API_KEY.

faq.question: When does the optional CLI need network access?
faq.answer: Live CLI generation and editing contact the OpenAI Image API. Dry runs do not make API requests.

faq.question: Can it create transparent images?
faq.answer: Yes. Transparency support depends on the selected tool and model, so the final alpha channel should be validated.

faq.question: Can it generate SVG or other vector files?
faq.answer: No. This skill targets raster images. Use native vector tools for deterministic SVG assets and established icon systems.
